lead.t: Immune‑complex small vessel (IgA vasculitis, cryoglobulinaemic): Oral glucocorticoids; add mycophenolate mofetil if renal involvement is severe — Hydroxychloroquine for skin/joint disease; treat underlying infection (e.g., hepatitis C)

Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) is a
less toxic alternative to cyclophosphamide.
Maintenance therapy: Azathioprine, methotrexate and MMF are
used for maintenance.

The latter group is typically managed with anti proliferative drugs (e.g. azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil), cal cineurin inhibitors (e.g. ciclosporin, tacrolimus), corticosteroids (e.g.\nprednisolone) or sirolimus.
cmn regimen is triple therapy with prednisolone; cyclosporine or tacrolimus; and azathioprine or mycophenolate mofetil(MMF).
Long‑term immunosuppression – corticosteroids (prednisone‑type) → steroid‑sparing agents (azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine)

Maintain remission / steroid‑sparing: Azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, methotrexate — Renal disease, musculoskeletal disease, steroid toxicity — Mycophenolate preferred for proliferative nephritis; azathioprine for milder disease
*Answer*: Start a steroid‑sparing immunosuppressant such as mycophenolate mofetil (preferred for class III/IV nephritis).
Moderate–severe disease warrants early introduction of disease‑modifying agents (mycophenolate mofetil, cyclophosphamide, or newer antifibrotics) and close monitoring for organ complications.
